source: Exported from Goodreads shelf https://www.goodreads.com/review/list/181752708 on 2026-09-04, refreshed later the same day to include newly added books
notes: Each category below is a direct pull of Tyler's Goodreads custom shelf of the same name. Books tagged 'do-not-recommend' on Goodreads have already been removed from these lists (see excluded_do_not_recommend).
'have_to_read' = true means Tyler also tagged the book on his Goodreads 'have-to-read' shelf. Treat these as the must-read standouts within a category (e.g. a gold border or badge).
'rating' is Tyler's own star rating (1-5) on Goodreads, not the public average. null means he read it but never rated it.
'review' is Tyler's own Goodreads review text where he wrote one; Goodreads truncates long reviews with '...more' in list view, so a few of these are partial. null means no review text.

The Holy Bible: King James Version is on Tyler's 'have-to-read' shelf but was never assigned to any of the four site categories on Goodreads, so it isn't included below. Flag this for Tyler in case he wants to add it to a category.

'The Warded Man' (adult-read, 1 star) has a personal review noting disturbing sexual-violence content, but Tyler did NOT tag it do-not-recommend on Goodreads. Kept in the data as-is since that's what his shelf says, but worth Tyler double-checking before it goes on a family gift site.
'Demon Copperhead' is tagged did-not-finish + adult-read on Goodreads, not actually 'read'. Excluded from the adult-read list below since it's not a completed recommendation.
Author names have been converted from Goodreads' 'Last, First' format to 'First Last' for display.

This file was refreshed later the same day to pick up new Goodreads additions. A Darkness at Sethanon, Blood of Tyrants, Crucible of Gold, and Empire of Ivory were added to Tyler's read shelf and rated (4, 3, 3, and 3 stars) but were not shelved into any of the four category shelves, so they are intentionally left out of every category below. Ask Tyler before adding them if that was an oversight.
The Book of Mormon is unusual: Tyler shelved it into junior-read, highschool-level, AND adult-read at once (plus have-to-read), so it appears in all three of those category lists below.
